headline: A six-month-old chip start-up with no product yet is reportedly raising funds at a valuation of about $2.5 billion.
score_reason: Exclusive based on two anonymous sources about a round that has not closed.
importance_line: Shows investors again paying billion-dollar prices for AI chip start-ups before they have a product, which matters to Intel and AMD, the long-time leaders in data center processors; the figures come from anonymous sources and could change.
summary: Reuters reports, citing two people familiar with the fundraising, that Nuvacore, a San Jose start-up backed by Sequoia Capital that is designing a central processor (CPU) for data centers, is raising hundreds of millions of dollars at a valuation of roughly $2.5 billion. The round has not closed and the people cautioned that its size and valuation could change; Reuters links the interest to rising demand for CPUs, which direct traffic for Nvidia's AI chips and run AI software agents.
notes: Original Reuters page blocked (401); text read on Devdiscourse and ET CIO copies of the Reuters story.
